title: The Wi-Fi Dashboard: access points, SSIDs and their metrics

prose.text: The Wi-Fi Dashboard is the console view of access point and SSID performance. {{purpose}} {{subscription}}

prose.label: Privacy settings.
prose.text: {{privacy-collection}} Whether the article means the Client Connector switch or the operating system's own permission is open {{gap:privacy-setting-meaning}}.

checks.do: Whether Collect Location Info for ZDX is enabled in Client Connector before treating an empty SSID or BSSID in the Wi-Fi Dashboard as a data fault.

purpose.statement: The Wi-Fi Dashboard uses existing user and device Wi-Fi data in the organization to monitor device performance, which can help identify locations where users might have issues with their Wi-Fi access points.

quotes: The Wi-Fi Dashboard utilizes existing user and device Wi-Fi data in your organization to monitor device performance. This data can help identify specific locations in which users might have issues with their Wi-Fi access points.

subscription.statement: Monitoring the Wi-Fi Dashboard needs a ZDX subscription level that supports it; the subscription table lists Wi-Fi as not supported on Standard and Microsoft 365 and supported on Advanced and Advanced Plus.

quotes: Your Digital Experience (ZDX) subscription level supports monitoring the Wi-Fi Dashboard.
| Wi-Fi | Not supported | Not supported | Supported | Supported |
| Feature | Standard | Microsoft 365 | Advanced | Advanced Plus |

range-filters.statement: The Wi-Fi Dashboard's time range runs from the previous 2 hours to 48 hours, or a custom range within the last 14 days. Its SSID filter takes up to 5 SSIDs and selects the SSID with the most devices by default, and its AP Prefix filter takes up to 6 prefixed characters.

quotes: Time range options are available in increments from the previous 2 Hours to 48 Hours, or a Custom Range within the last 14 Days.
You can select up to 5 SSIDs from the drop-down menu. The SSID associated with the highest number of devices is selected by default.
AP Prefix: Enter up to 6 prefixed characters to filter access points.

privacy-collection.statement: When Client Connector's Collection Location Info for ZDX is not enabled, privacy information for Wi-Fi details such as SSID and BSSID is not captured in the Wi-Fi Dashboard. The article also says certain operating systems with the latest updates, for example macOS and Windows 11, do not enable Client Connector's privacy settings by default.

quotes: When Zscaler Client Connector's Collection Location Info for ZDX is not enabled, privacy information for Wi-Fi details, such as SSID and BSSID, are not captured in the Wi-Fi Dashboard.
Certain operating systems (e.g., macOS, Windows 11), with the latest updates, do not enable Zscaler Client Connector's privacy settings by default.

overview-widgets.statement: The dashboard shows the current number of active access points and of active devices, each with its percentage change over the selected period, and distributes access points and connected devices by Good, Okay and Poor ZDX Scores. It estimates active devices per Wi-Fi band, with the device count duplicated for any device using more than one Wi-Fi band at a given time, and lists the top 5 geolocations by connected devices.

quotes: Total Access Points: The current number of active access points with a percentage increase or decrease over the selected time period.
Wi-Fi Performance of Access Points: A performance distribution based on Good, Okay, and Poor ZDX Scores.
Total Devices Connected: The current number of active devices with a percentage increase or decrease over the selected time period.
ZDX Score Distribution: The distribution of Good, Okay, and Poor ZDX Scores for all connected devices.

Wi-Fi Band Distribution: The estimated number of total active devices delineated by Wi-Fi band percentage. The device count is duplicated for any device using more than one Wi-Fi band at a given time.
Top Geolocations by Devices Connected: The top 5 geolocations with the highest device counts, along with the distribution of their respective ZDX Scores.

ap-views.statement: Wi-Fi performance by geolocation can be switched between a map view and a list view, and a location's access points show by default as a tree view whose tile color follows a ZDX Score and whose tile size follows user volume. The access point list gives the MAC address, a custom name, the number of users and devices, and average latency and jitter in milliseconds, and an access point's info can be customized with the Edit icon.

quotes: Wi-Fi Performance by Geolocation: The SSID performance distribution via location. You can switch between Map View or List View.
The default Tree View of a location's access points is color-coded according to Wi-Fi performance, with each tile color based on a ZDX Score.
The size of each tile is based on user volume, with the largest user count shown on the left side of the page, and the lowest user count shown towards the right side of the page.
MAC Address: The access point identifier.
Custom Name: If applicable, the customized name for the access point.
Number of Users: The total count of active users connected to the access point.
Number of Devices: The total count of active devices connected to the access point.
Avg Latency: The average latency of the access point, measured in milliseconds.
Avg Jitter: The average jitter of the access point, measured in milliseconds.
You can also click the Edit icon to customize the access point info.

ap-details.statement: An access point's details give source-to-gateway latency and jitter over the selected range, its AP MAC and active users and devices, and for each connected device the BSSID, Wi-Fi adapter, ZDX Score, average signal strength, Wi-Fi type and Wi-Fi channel.

quotes: Source to Gateway Latency: The average time for a data packet to travel from the source device to the gateway within the selected time range.
Source to Gateway Jitter: The average variation in latency between data packets traveling from the source device to the gateway within the selected time range.
AP MAC: The MAC address of the access point.
Active Users: The number of active users and devices connected to the access point within the selected time range.
A table that identifies each user connected to the access point provides additional Wi-Fi information.
Device: A user's device connected to the access point.
BSSID: The Basic Service Set Identifier.
Wi-Fi Adapter: The adapter brand of the access point.
ZDX Score: The score for the device connected to the access point.
Signal Strength: The average Wi-Fi signal strength of the device.
Wi-Fi Type: The wireless communication standard of the access point.
Wi-Fi Channel: The channel number associated with the band frequency.

alternative-metrics.statement: Wi-Fi data collection can optionally be configured to use signal strength and retransmission rate, instead of ZDX Score, to identify low-performing Wi-Fi devices.

quotes: Optionally, you can configure your Wi-Fi data collection to use signal strength and retransmission rate to identify low-performing Wi-Fi devices instead of ZDX Score.

privacy-setting-meaning.title: Whether the Wi-Fi article's privacy settings are Client Connector's switch or the operating system's permission
privacy-setting-meaning.detail: The Wi-Fi article says Client Connector's Collection Location Info for ZDX must be enabled for SSID and BSSID, and that certain operating systems with the latest updates do not enable Client Connector's privacy settings by default. The Client Connector User Privacy article says its ZDX location setting is enabled by default, [[zcc.web-privacy.collection:zdx-location]]. The Wi-Fi wording names Client Connector's privacy settings, but may mean the operating system's own location permission for Client Connector; neither article says.
